Jordan (Solutions): Heads-up - SierraHealth asked for a Private/VPC design for a 30-day POC. Requirements: private connectivity, static outbound IPs for allowlists, ability to prove per-request logs, and an item in their security questionnaire about preserving original client IPs.
Priya (NetEng): Quick check 1: Do they mandate client src-ip preservation, or just for audit metadata? That changes whether we recommend VPC peering vs PrivateLink.
Jordan (Solutions): They said 'preserve client IPs for audit trails' but are open to app-level headers if we document the limitation. Their security team prefers not to accept cross-account peering if it can be avoided.
Dana (AE): Pricing Q: POC estimate for 2 static EIPs, single AZ PrivateDeploy, and 2 vCPU load balancer for 30 days? Also any setup fees for a private endpoint?
Carlos (Security): We need to answer: (a) can customer use their KMS/HSM for key storage in PrivateDeploy, (b) do we support VPC Flow Logs export, (c) how do we surface per-tenant request logs securely?
Priya (NetEng): Short answers: (a) Yes, customer-managed KMS via cross-account IAM role is supported in PrivateDeploy; HSMs via partners (we should note supported vendors). (b) Yes, we can forward VPC Flow Logs and host audit logs to the customer's S3 or CloudWatch via role. (c) We can emit request-level logs with a request-id header and export segregated log streams per-tenant; retention depends on plan. I'll write this into the questionnaire.
Jordan (Solutions): Great. Also they have TLS-inspect at their perimeter and need SNI allowlist guidance and MTU guidance for any S2S tunnels.
Priya (NetEng): SNI allowlist snippet (customer perimeter):
```
# perimeter SNI allowlist example
allow tcp any 443 to 34.121.198.0/24   # Redwood Private endpoints (AZ range example)
match tls.sni == "sierra-api.svc.redwood.ai" -> allow
```
Priya (NetEng): Note: if customer terminates TLS and re-encrypts, they must preserve SNI or validate the certs we present. For peering (no TLS termination), SNI not needed.
Carlos (Security): For audit, app-level X-Forwarded-For is acceptable if we can attest to header integrity. Recommend mTLS between their egress proxy and our endpoint if they require header authenticity.
Jordan (Solutions): Good call. SierraHealth also asked whether a Dedicated pool option can provide static egress without losing src-ip.
Priya (NetEng): Dedicated pool + NAT EIP preserves outbound IP but still NATs internal clients behind the NAT - original client private IPs will not be preserved across the NAT. To preserve src IPs you need a route path (peering) that carries original packets. But peering requires both accounts to accept route propagation and security controls.
Dana (AE): Customer is risk-averse to peering. How do we present the trade-offs succinctly for the decision maker?
Priya (NetEng): Two short bullet options:
- PrivateLink-first (recommended if customer avoids peering): simple to approve, endpoint controlled by customer, preserves isolation. Outbound static EIP: achievable via Dedicated PrivateDeploy or customer-run egress proxy. Original client IP: not preserved; use X-Forwarded-For + mTLS for authenticity.
- Peering-first (recommended if client IP must be preserved): preserves original src IPs across the path, lower obs on TLS-SNI if traffic stays L3. Requires cross-account peering approval and route controls, slightly more operational overhead.
Jordan (Solutions): Dana - can you confirm whether SierraHealth can stand up an egress proxy in their VPC for the POC? That would be the easiest way to get stable outbound IPs without Dedicated.
Dana (AE): I'll ask and get back in the call.
Priya (NetEng): Tunnel recommendations for SD-WAN/S2S: enable BFD for sub-500ms failover, set MTU 1400 and enable MSS clamp on the tunnel endpoints. Example ipsec fragment adjustment:
```
# recommended ipsec settings
set mtu 1400
set mss-adjust 1360
enable bfd interval 50 min_rx 50 multiplier 3
```
Jordan (Solutions): InfraBot - can you attach the POC network checklist and the AKS/EC2 footprints for PrivateDeploy?
InfraBot: POC network checklist and PrivateDeploy sizing docs added: https://redwood.internal/handbook/poc-network-checklist, https://redwood.internal/handbook/privatedeploy-sizing (access: redwood employees).
Carlos (Security): Add to questionnaire: provide SOC2 link, encryption in transit details, and certificate renewal process. We'll also include a short note on HSM partners for FIPS workloads.
Priya (NetEng): Firewall snippet for outbound allowlist (customer side) so they can restrict egress to just our POC endpoints:
```
# customer egress example
allow tcp any 443 to 34.121.198.12   # single PrivateLink ENI (AZ1)
allow tcp any 443 to 34.121.198.13   # PrivateLink ENI (AZ2)
allow udp any 53 to 10.0.0.2         # dns resolver
```
Jordan (Solutions): Dana - timeline: scheduled demo + handoff call Wed 11am PT. Before then we need: (1) answer to whether they can run egress proxy (2) KMS/HSM details added to questionnaire (3) pricing for: PrivateDeploy POC (30d) with 2 EIPs, Dedicated option monthly pro-rata, and peering onboarding fee if applicable.
Dana (AE): Will confirm egress proxy and budget. I'll upload initial quote and attach SOC2.
Carlos (Security): I'll drop the HSM partner names and quick notes into the questionnaire (Gemini HSM, VendorX appliance via partner).
Priya (NetEng): Final: include a short fallback plan in the doc - if peering is blocked we recommend: PrivateLink + customer egress proxy OR Dedicated NAT EIP (we manage) + XFF. Also indicate expected differences in latency (peering slightly lower latency than PrivateLink due to L3 path).
Jordan (Solutions): Thanks all. Action items: Priya -> questionnaire network answers & SNI/MTU snippets; Carlos -> security/HSM + SOC2 attachments; Dana -> customer confirmation on egress proxy & budget; Jordan -> compile POC one-pager and send invite.
Dana (AE): ack
Priya (NetEng): ack :white_check_mark:
Carlos (Security): ack
Jordan (Solutions): I'll run the invite now.
